pr_title: Fix incorrect String type hint for @export
pr_body:
Fixes #42022

Now `@export`ing a `String` displays a `LineEdit` in the inspector as in 3.2.

One can use `@export_type_string` to get the node type selection popup
pr_comments: The fix is okay, I'm just not sure if we need the `@export_type_string` annotation. Is it actually useful for something?
I have no idea, I just replicated what was already possible in case someone needs it.

My plan is to add a custom export annotation that allows you to use any hint, which should be enough. In this case you don't really want the type to be String, it can be other types.

I now just realized that this fix was already included in #47131 (sorry, I didn't realize at the time there was open PR already). Not sure why this isn't reporting any conflict.

issue_context.title: Plainly exported strings default to type string hints in GDScript 2.0
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
4566db2a


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10 Home Edition


**Issue description:**
When attempting to export a string variable in GDScript, as one would have done in GDScript 1, rather than display a LineEdit, it displays a GUI in the Inspector that has you select an Object type to assign to the string value. This appears to be because the `@export` annotation hardcodes the property hint to be `PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING` when I really don't want any sort of type specification.

We can fix it by properly creating appropriate export annotations for each case, since it appears that we are creating dedicated export annotations for every used hint string and not bothering with any sort of export inference.

1. `@export` which just exports things plainly and uses `PROPERTY_HINT_NONE`.
1. `@export_type_string(str)` which does what `@export` currently does.

**Steps to reproduce:**

```gdscript
extends Resource
class_name MyData
@export
var name := "hello"
```

Then, create a new MyData in the Inspector to see the result.


**Minimal reproduction project:**
The steps are trivial enough that it isn't necessary.

review_comments: I'm not sure what's the use case for this export hint, or whether the name properly conveys it. I think the hint for `@export` was a bug, not an intended feature, so it may not need to be kept.
I'm surprised that `&GDScriptParser::export_annotations<PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING, Variant::STRING>` makes it an export hint for selecting an Object type though, that's pretty weird.

To be honest I didn't think too much about this, but I agree that I found it strange to have an object type selection. I never saw this in 3.2 but maybe it was already possible and I missed it. Maybe we should get feedback from whoever added that "feature"
